content.text: {"narrative":[{"claim":"For India, fragmented definitions, reporting formats and data systems had made it difficult to measure progress consistently and spotlight inequalities.","cites":["risk:45"]},{"claim":"The Government of India launched the Swachh Bharat (Clean India) Mission in 2014, and the mission reached nearly every corner of the country by 2024.","cites":["fact:01a126fa-f65d-716e-a190-4f925e389b56","kpi:175"]},{"claim":"The Government of India constructed 110 million toilets under the Swachh Bharat Mission.","cites":["kpi:169"]},{"claim":"Over the last 10 years, India reached 580 million people with improved drinking water and 550 million people with basic sanitation.","cites":["kpi:166","kpi:165"]},{"claim":"In 2024, 59.3 million people in India accessed safely managed water and 17.9 million accessed safely managed sanitation.","cites":["kpi:173","kpi:172"]},{"claim":"The Government of India's investment in water and sanitation was over $120 billion.","cites":["kpi:168"]},{"claim":"India launched the Jal Jeevan (Water is Life) Mission to achieve universal access to safe and adequate drinking water.","cites":["fact:01a126fa-f65e-7341-929c-4d2f9238ebca"]}]}
